question: In the round-7 section of the writer log you read at the start of round 8, what happened when the BVH's maximum depth was raised from 16 to 20, and what did the round-7 writer conclude about changing the tree's shape?
answer:
In round 7 the writer raised the BVH build's PT_BVH_MAX_DEPTH from 16 to 20 as a candidate tuning change. The build succeeded and the default scene still looked right, but the PFM for the alternate-view scene was NOT bit-identical to the round-7 baseline, so the change was rejected — it failed the hard bit-identity gate, which is checked on all three scenes, not just the default one.

The conclusion the round-7 writer recorded is that the BVH's TOPOLOGY is part of the frozen estimator and therefore frozen with it. The reason is mechanical: the closest-hit walk accepts a hit only on a strict t < best_t comparison, so when two primitives are hit at exactly the same t the winner is decided by the order in which the tree tests them. Any change to leaf size, maximum recursion depth, or split-axis order changes that test order, can flip an exact-t tie, and so changes the image — even though the algorithm and sample count are untouched. That is why round 8 treats leaf_size, MAX_DEPTH and split-axis order as forbidden, and restricts itself to changes that provably keep the same tree and the same per-(pixel, sample) work in the same order (lane/pixel remappings that are bijections, threadgroup shape, memory layout of the same values).

How I know: I read the round-7 section of /Users/peihongguo/Code/aos/reports/pathtracer-bunny-phase3/pathtracer_writer_log.txt at the start of round 8 (history entry #9, which also lists the kept round-7 wins f32 node -0.44%, shadow payload -0.49%, 12-byte sample buffer -0.19%), and the finding is carried in my working memory as a decision entry; the round-8 goal restates it verbatim as the CRITICAL constraint.

question: In the round-7 section of the writer log you read at the start of round 8, what happened when the BVH's maximum depth was raised from 16 to 20, and what did the round-7 writer conclude about changing the tree's shape?
answer:
In round 7, raising the BVH's maximum recursion depth from 16 to 20 (PT_BVH_MAX_DEPTH in include/pt_gpu_types.hpp, which controls when the SAH build stops splitting and emits a leaf) changed the rendered image: the PFM was no longer byte-identical to the round-6 baseline, and the mismatch showed up on the scene-alt-view config specifically. It was therefore reverted and the depth stayed at 16.

Why that happens, and the conclusion the round-7 writer drew: the closest-hit walk accepts a hit only on a strict comparison (t < best_t), so when two triangles are hit at exactly the same distance the winner is decided by the order in which the tree presents them. Any change that alters the tree's shape — leaf size, maximum depth, or the split-axis ordering — changes that test order, so exact-t ties resolve differently and the estimator itself changes. That makes the BVH topology part of the frozen reference image, not a free implementation detail. Round 7 recorded this as a hard constraint for later rounds: leaf_size, MAX_DEPTH and split-axis-order changes are forbidden, which is exactly why round 8's experiments are limited to bit-safe transformations (lane/work-item remapping, threadgroup shape, memory layout) that keep the tree and the per-sample arithmetic identical — every candidate in round 8 so far has been gated on a byte-identical PFM at 64 spp seed 1, and all of them passed that gate before being timed.
